defect.description: Isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO) never matches a real file: typing.TextIO is not a base class of what open() returns (io.TextIOWrapper, or the io.BufferedWriter of the default os.devnull log), so stop() still leaves every file log open, as before; it should test io.IOBase (or for a close method).

review_items: isinstance(self.log_output, TextIO) misses the default os.devnull BufferedWriter, leaking the handle; check IO[Any] or hasattr close instead
Removing except Exception: pass means os.close() failures now propagate from stop(); is that intended?
IO and Any imports are unused after the change; drop them
votes.evidence_quote: When `log_output` is `None`, `__init__` line 23 opens `os.devnull` in binary mode (`"wb"`), producing a `BufferedWriter`. That is **not** a `TextIO` instance, so `close()` is never called and the file handle leaks on every service that uses the default.
votes.justification: The review flags the right isinstance(TextIO) check in stop() and proposes the right fix (check for a close method). It catches the leak only for the default os.devnull BufferedWriter. It wrongly says text-mode files opened from a path are TextIO and close correctly, so it misses that typing.TextIO never matches any real file object.
